description:
Hi! My name is Aashni Aggarwal, and I am studying in 9th grade in India. I have special interest in the fields of Geology, Planetary Science, and Space Exploration. I would describe myself as a creative and passionate person, who has an interest in creating new things.

For the NASA space apps challenge, I combined my interests in various fields to develop an optical and topographic terrain map for the Martian Jezero Crater region.
summary:
PROJECT OVERVIEW:
I have created a map interface a Mars astronaut could use during a surface exploration mission, using NASA data and tools. This project covers the Jezero crater region, which has been observed by the Perseverance rover, but still requires a thorough on site exploration by humans physically. To create an interactive map which astronauts could take with them, I have combined topographic and optical data.

THE CHALLENGE:
Navigating the Martian terrain is a tough task, especially while carrying out operations with human astronauts where lives are at risk. The martian topography is ever varying and challenging.

SOLUTION:
I have made a Martian Maps dashboard that shows topographic elevation and slope data in the form of a high resolution visual map. It also shows the optical data in the form of images taken by the Perseverance rover and other machines at critical sites. This will allow the astronauts to easily identify the terrain and their surroundings and to plan beforehand based on the places of intended travel.

IMPACT ON SPACE EXPLORATION:
While multiple rovers are sent to various Martian parts for research and analysis, sending humans to Mars requires an unbelievable amount of data for operations to be successful. By embedding images directly into maps as well, this dashboard creates the potential for ground level visualization as well, allowing astronauts to truly understand what they will see from the human perspective.
details:
THE CHALLENGE

Navigating the Martian terrain is a tough task, especially while carrying out operations with human astronauts where lives are at risk. The martian topography is ever varying and challenging, especially in regions of interest where scientific research can be done such as the Jezero crater.

SOLUTION

I have made a Martian Maps dashboard that shows topographic elevation and slope data (from credible digital elevation models DTMs) in the form of a high resolution visual map. It also shows the optical data in the form of images taken by the Perseverance rover and other machines at critical sites such as The base of Jezero Crater Delta, The “Bright Angel” area of Jezero crater, The scarp along delta in Jezero crater, and the fan shaped deposits visible from the Octavia E. Butler landing site. This will allow the astronauts to easily identify the terrain and their surroundings and to plan beforehand based on the places of intended travel.

IMPACT ON SPACE EXPLORATION

While multiple rovers are sent to various Martian parts for research and analysis, sending humans to Mars requires an unbelievable amount of data for operations to be successful. By embedding images directly into maps as well, this dashboard creates the potential for ground level visualization as well, allowing astronauts to truly understand what they will see from the human perspective.

WHY JEZERO CRATER?

Jezero Crater has always been a place of interest on the Martian surface for me and many. It has been selected as the landing site for the Perseverance rover due to geological evidence indicating that it was once a river delta. The delta deposits near the crater are suitable for finding preserved biosignatures or signs of life from earlier years of Martian history.

METHODOLOGY & TECHNICAL WORKFLOW

  1. Data: This project used vast amounts of specialized data from the precise Jezero crater region. I used authentic NASA/USGS Digital Terrain Models(DTMS) to establish acute elevation and slope details.
  2. QGIS Usage: I used QGIS to process Raster datasets to calculate precise surface slope angles and generate the final interactive visual.
  3. Waypoint Images: To add images to the waypoints, I integrated the project with Images from Perseverance by linking the waypoints to web links to the NASA website, showing the images for the coordinates chosen. I utilized the vast NASA Image library.

INNOVATION AND UNIQUENESS

This project map does not rely on flat 2d maps and separate maps not combining multiple useful data. This project helps astronauts to actually get information they need in real time. The project integrates multi layered spatial synchronization, combining accurate and precise Digital Elevation Models (DTMs). The project provides a unified place for the workspace that can be deployed even using open source tools.

FUTURE SCALABILITY POTENTIAL

This project has immense potential as in the future it can seamlessly be integrated with even more data, including types like essential radiation data and live atmospheric data as well. Automated algorithms can be added that can help by suggest possible safe routes and paths for astronauts.
